newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch plan 25 percent cut in pig numbers in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Dutch plan 25 percent cut in pig numbers in 1998.

text.p: Dutch Farm Ministry said on Thursday it planned to cut the country's population of pigs next year by a quarter in response to the recent swine fever epidemic.
The plan, intended to make the sector more manageable, will mean a reduction of around four million pigs nationwide but there will be no active cull, a spokewoman said.
Minister Jozias van Aartsen has earmarked 475 million guilders to realize the plan.
"The minister believes now is the time to act. There is an enormous problem swine fever," she said.
She said that under the plan, legislation would be initiated during 1998 which would require each pig farm to cut its numbers by the required 25 percent.
"This is not an active cull. The number of pigs will be reduced by the normal slaughtering process," she added.
Almost 330 cases of swine fever have appeared in the Netherlands since the outbreak first appeared in February.
Despite strict controls on the transportation of pigs, the highly contagious disease has continued to spread, prompting many countries to ban the import of Dutch pigs and pork meat.
